question: A hyperdense middle cerebral artery (MCA) sign on non-contrast CT brain represents acute thrombus within the MCA and may be the only CT abnormality in the first 1–2 hours of ischaemic stroke.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The hyperdense MCA sign is caused by acute thrombus in the MCA, which is denser than flowing blood on NCCT. It can be the sole CT abnormality in the hyperacute window and should prompt consideration of CT angiography and mechanical thrombectomy.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The hyperdense MCA sign reflects the high density of fresh clot and is one of the earliest CT signs of MCA territory ischaemia, often preceding any parenchymal change. Recognising it is clinically important as it identifies a large-vessel occlusion amenable to thrombectomy.
